incident.name: Citizens Bank + Frost Bank Dual Breach
incident.description: Everest ransomware posted both Citizens Financial ($228B assets) and Frost Bank ($53B assets) on the same day — both breached via a single shared vendor. Matching document metadata confirmed shared point of failure. Federal class-action lawsuits filed within days.
incident.root_cause: Shared third-party vendor with access to multiple financial institutions, no vendor isolation
incident.lessons: Shared vendors create shared, invisible risk. Financial institutions must assess and isolate vendor access paths continuously.

relatedIncidents.name: Equifax Data Breach
relatedIncidents.description: Unpatched Apache Struts vulnerability exposed PII of 147M Americans including SSNs, DOBs, and credit card numbers.
relatedIncidents.root_cause: Unpatched known vulnerability (2 months old), poor asset inventory
relatedIncidents.lessons: Patch management and asset inventory are foundational security controls.

relatedIncidents.name: Lazarus Group Bangladesh Bank Heist
relatedIncidents.description: $81M stolen from Bangladesh Bank via fraudulent SWIFT messages. $951M attempted. Exploited weak SWIFT security controls.
relatedIncidents.root_cause: Weak SWIFT security controls, no anomaly detection on transactions
relatedIncidents.lessons: Financial transaction monitoring and SWIFT security controls are critical.

relatedIncidents.name: Bybit Crypto Heist
relatedIncidents.description: Lazarus Group compromised the Safe{Wallet} multisig interface used by Bybit, injecting malicious JavaScript to redirect a $1.5B ETH transfer. Largest crypto theft in history.
relatedIncidents.root_cause: Supply chain compromise of third-party wallet UI, insufficient transaction verification
relatedIncidents.lessons: Crypto platforms must verify transaction destinations out-of-band. Third-party UI dependencies are critical attack surfaces.
